_policy: English sources are preferred (see REQUIREMENTS.md > RSS source(s)). A source is only acceptable if it is (1) reachable, (2) serving current dates, and (3) carrying real article text rather than titles only. Run `python fetcher/fetch_rss.py --check-sources` to apply that test to every entry here.
_deployment: Production runs on an OVERSEAS VPS where all of these feeds are reachable directly - there is no GFW constraint in production. Local development is behind the GFW and sees a much smaller subset, so DO NOT pick sources by local reachability. Re-run `--check-sources` on the VPS before trusting any verdict here: staleness and empty summaries are network-independent and are the checks that actually matter.
_proxy: Local-testing convenience only. Default "auto" (env vars, and on Windows the WinINET registry, which is how a local VPN is picked up) | "none" for a direct connection | an explicit http://host:port. A VPS needs no proxy. The resolved value is logged on every run.

_active_set: Six sources: CGTN (China, state), Al Jazeera (Qatar, state-funded), BBC (UK, public), Guardian (UK, independent), SCMP (Hong Kong, Alibaba-owned), NYT (US). Chosen for a mix of state-affiliated and independent outlets, since a single source measurably skewed the sentiment breadth (70% positive alone vs ~30% across the set). Two consequences the index inherits from this choice, both measured rather than assumed: volume is very uneven (Guardian 34% and SCMP 25% are 59% of the corpus between them) and the outlets disagree sharply (mean signed impact from +0.76 for CGTN to -1.11 for NYT - a span of 1.87, on a scale where the index responds to differences of about 0.2). So the mood is not invariant to which outlet happens to publish most: dropping Guardian moves S(t) about +26%, dropping SCMP about -18%, both larger than the entire drift the index showed in its first three weeks. That is a property of the instrument. Remaining disabled candidates: npr-world, cna, chinanews-world, solidot.
_divergence_note: 2026-10-09: the deployed copy on the VPS had scmp and nyt-world ENABLED while this file had them disabled, so production measured six sources while the repo declared four - and b (-0.4991) was calibrated on that six-source corpus, i.e. partly on sources this file claimed were off. Reconciled by enabling both here. This file is pushed by hand (deploy/README.md: scp fetcher/fetch_rss.py fetcher/feeds.json go4pro:rpi/fetcher/), so the repo and the VPS can drift silently - verify with the fetcher's own log line 'reading N feed(s) from ...'.
_max_items_note: Cap on items taken per feed per poll. In steady state it is irrelevant - only ~3 new items per feed appear between hourly polls - but on the first run after a change it decides how far back the index history reaches. The feeds expose cgtn 50, guardian 45, bbc 27, aljazeera 25 items, so 50 takes everything available and backfills as far as each feed's window allows (roughly 4-6 days). The cost is one-off: extra items are analysed once, then cached. GOTCHA: a per-feed "max_items" OVERRIDES this global value, so setting only the global while a feed entry still carries its own silently does nothing.
